correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and n mod 4 in {0,3}, the pinned RESULT proves an elementary simplicial collapse of the independence complex after deleting a single antipodal rung, not merely a homology vanishing. Its selected vertices Z consist of the now nonadjacent rung endpoints in column 0 and disjoint surviving even rungs, so Ind(G[Z])=Delta^1*(S^0)^r. For each nonempty independent exterior T, adjacency blocking gives an available isolated selected endpoint unless both deleted-rung endpoints and every chosen even-rung pair are symmetrically blocked; the parity propagation forces incompatible rail choices at the twisted seam, in both residue classes (including n=3). The fiberwise toggle is a complete acyclic matching; exterior sets weakly descend along unmatched edges, so a closed gradient path cannot mix fibers. This proves relative collapse to Ind(G[Z]), which is itself a ball with a simplex factor. Independently rebuilt modular graphs and tested every nonempty independent exterior face for n=3,4,7,8,11,12, obtaining respectively 6,8,62,80,566,728 faces with cone toggles and no counterexample; all-parameter proof, not finite enumeration, carries the theorem.
residual_risks: No fully formalized machine-checked acyclic matching for arbitrary n; uniform parity and patchwork criteria were inspected by hand.
No multi-rung, rim-fault or equivariant assertion follows.

Simple collapsibility supplies an explicit combinatorial strong result, not a routine numerical Betti computation or rewording of the complementary noncontractible theorem. The cone-fiber and twisted-seam parity mechanism may be reused for graph-fault comparisons.
